name: Cheverny

limits: For white wine, Sauvignon Blanc and Sauvignon Gris together: 60 to 84%
For white wine, Chardonnay, Chenin Blanc and Orbois together: 16 to 40%
For red and rosé wine, Pinot Noir: 60 to 84%
For red and rosé wine, Gamay: 16 to 40%
For red and rosé wine, Malbec: at most 5%
rules.yield_base: 60 hl/ha for white, 55 for red and rosé

climate.koppen_name: Temperate, no dry season, warm summer

climate: Sauvignon Blanc and Pinot Noir sit in their sweet spot, so the wines can show the style they are known for.

terms: France's protected place names. A wine sold under one must follow that appellation's rules. The EU's term for the same tier is PDO, or AOP in French.

blurb.text: A Loire Valley appellation for dry white, light red and rosé wines. Whites are led by Sauvignon Blanc, blended with other grapes. It spreads over communes of Loir-et-Cher and became an AOC in 1993.
